messages.content: Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

output:
Here's a draft. Bracketed bits are the details I don't have — swap them in and the word count lands right around 250.

---

**Subject: [Service name] moves to [new platform] on [date]**

Hi [name],

We're moving [Service name] onto [new platform] during Q[N]. The cutover starts [date] and finishes [date].

Why bother? The current stack has been running since [year], and it's showing its age — [specific pain: overnight batch jobs that take 6 hours, an API that rate-limits at 100 requests a minute, no way to export your own data]. We could keep patching it. We'd rather not.

What changes for you:

- Your sign-in stays the same. Same email, same password, same SSO setup if you use it.
- [Feature X] gets a new URL: [old] becomes [new]. Old links redirect until [date].
- [Feature Y] works differently — [one sentence on how]. We've written it up at [link].
- Integrations built on API v[N] keep working through [date]. After that, v[N+1] only. Migration notes: [link].

What you need to do before [date]:

1. [Concrete action, e.g. re-authorize your Slack integration]
2. [Concrete action, e.g. download any reports older than 12 months]

If you do nothing, your account still moves. You'll just hit [specific consequence] on the other side.

Expect [X hours] of downtime on [date, time, timezone]. We'll post live status at [status page link].

Questions go to [email] or [support channel]. If you're on an enterprise plan, your account manager can walk your team through it — just ask.

— [Name], [Title]

---

Two things worth deciding before you send: whether to name the pain point honestly (I'd argue yes — customers already feel it), and whether the downtime window is firm enough to commit to in writing.
